title: Inciting incident (12-16 minutes):
use_cases: Use when establishing the transition from the normal world to the horror narrative
Implement when forcing a protagonist to make a choice that leads toward the primary conflict
Configure when introducing the first subtle indication of supernatural or violent activity
Use when developing internal character conflict through the theme of denial
content:
Something happens to shake up the normal world and trigger the horror. Often the main characters make a choice that puts them on a collision course with the ‘monster’. Sometimes they receive a warning to turn back, which they don’t heed. This is frequently the point at which they have their first encounter with the threat, but it is not full-on It’s just enough to give a clear indication that some sort of unnatural or violent activity is afoot.

Doubt and denial — the protagonists don’t realise the true danger of the choice they have made or the thing they have encountered. They will often try to make sense of what they saw or heard, or they’ll want to believe it was a figment of their imagination. If they relate their experience to others, the people around them may deny that the events ever took place.

Example: In “The Shining” (1980), Jack accepts the job as caretaker of the Overlook Hotel. Back home, Jack’s son Danny can sense that Jack’s decision is a bad one, but not just how bad.
